text:
nathan: FYI nightly e2e perf gate tripped on longseq p99, looks like a latency regression in the runner. p99 baseline ~120ms -> observed ~210ms on the nightly run :grimacing:

ci-bot: nightly-e2e-longseq-2623456789 failed perf-gate (p99 latency 210ms > threshold 150ms). Job: https://ci.redwood.example/builds/7642. Artifacts: https://ci.redwood.example/artifacts/7642/

nathan: stack trace / heatmap attached in artifacts. Quick glance: KV cache hit ratio dropped from ~98% to ~62% during the window, and we saw a burst of backend queueing on host gpu-18. Not sure if it's infra or runtime change.

jia: thanks for the heads up. can you paste the suspect commit(s) range? if it's infra, we should pause canary deployments. :eyes:

nathan: suspect range is between c3f9b2a..d1a7f4e (merged yesterday). No obvious runtime code touching caching, though d1a7f4e bumped the kernel selection timing.

alex: I can kick a rerun + bisect. prefer to run the nightly config but with e2e verbosity ON and KV logging to get precise hit/miss counts. nathan — can you post the exact command you want me to run?

nathan: run: 
```
./scripts/run_e2e.sh --profile longseq --repeat 3 --kvcache-logging=debug --artifact-bucket s3://redwood-e2e-debug/2623456789
```
Also please pin to commit d1a7f4e as the initial point for bisect (bisect will try earlier commits).

alex: starting rerun now, will report back in ~25m. if rerun matches regression we start git bisect across c3f9b2a..d1a7f4e.

maya: quick note — autoscaler had a warning in the same timeframe yesterday (pod churn in us-west2). could be noisy infra + the kernel timing bump amplifying misses. if bisect points to infra, I'll pull infra oncall.

ci-bot: rerun triggered by alex at 2623456940: https://ci.redwood.example/builds/7645 .

alex: rerun finished — latency still high on replicate 2, KV hit ratio low. starting bisect now.

nathan: thanks team. tagging @eng-oncall in case infra noise shows up in the bisect. keeping canary paused for now. :pray:

jia: ping me if bisect lands on anything touching kernel selection — I have a small repro to try locally.

alex: bisect progress: currently narrowed to d1a7f4e as the first bad. bisect script reproducible on our infra. next step: create a tiny reproducer with the same seq distribution and KV pattern.

maya: noted — I'll open an infra incident if we see pod churn correlating with the same timestamps in cluster logs.

nathan: filing a short follow-up ticket with links and adding the perf-run artifacts. thanks all.

(brief reactions: :eyes: x2, :thumbsup:)
